case_data.title: Belgian Citizens Panel on AI
case_data.provide-a-brief-description-of-the-proje:
The Belgian Citizens Panel was composed of 60 randomly selected citizens invited to take part in three weekends of learning and deliberation in the first part of 2024 related to the evolution of artificial intelligence in Europe.

The Panel was organized as part of the Belgian presidency of the European Union, and was the first time a citizens assembly has been organized in support of an EU presidency. 

Over three weekends between February and April 2024, participants came together and took part in multi-lingual deliberations, reflecting that Dutch and French are both official languages in Belgium. 

Following deliberation, the Panel's findings were shared at a launch event in Brussels. Over a three-hour session, members of the citizens panel presented their findings, and then took part in a series of discussions asking questions of invited guests, including members of the European Parliament, industry representatives, representatives of the Belgian EU Presidency and the Belgian Minister of the Interior, International Reform of Democratic Renewal.
case_data.inclusion-efforts:
The project report notes a number of inclusion measures.

"To eliminate as many barriers as possible, the following
measures were taken:

1\. Each participant received a fee of 320 euros (the fee was paid after participation in the full citizen panel).

2\. Free lunch, drinks and snacks were provided during the citizen panel.

3\. The participants’ dietary preferences were actively taken into account (vegetarian, vegan, halal, etc.)

4\. For parents with children under 12, professional child care was arranged.

5\. Any individuals requiring assistance and citizens who so wished, were allowed to bring a companion. The companion could also enjoy the catering provided but did not participate in the citizen panel.

6\. Participants younger than 18 were given permission to bring a parent/guardian.

7\. Participants who lived more than 100 km from Brussels were offered hotel stays and dinner each weekend, with guidance.

8\. First meeting in person: The organising team notified each citizen who had been drawn, by phone.

9, Four online information sessions were organised in two languages prior to the citizen panel.

10\. Before and during the citizen panel, a contact point was set up where citizens could ask questions at any time via phone, email, or WhatsApp.

11\. All the facilitators were experienced in working with a highly diverse target group, and made sure all citizens were well looked after, during the sessions and during the breaks.

12\. Each citizen could express him or herself in their own language throughout the process.

13\. A quiet room was provided for citizens who felt the need to be alone for a while.

The organisers report that these measures "resulted in 100% participation of the 60 citizens at the start of the citizen panel. Only three citizens dropped out during the process."

case_data.why-is-this-project-important-to-include:
This is the first example of a panel as part of the rotating presidency of the European Union. 

The final presentation event of the project involved panel members asking questions of power-holders, adding a strong communication element to the project. 

The process involved a number of methodological developments, including hands-on demonstrations of AI tools, and experiments with AI transcription.
project-goals: Qualitative: Capture qualitative evidence on public attitudes to AI

data.title:
The vision of this citizen panel is that the EU should build and strengthen its position in the world as follows (2/2):

Making decisions more rapidly to keep pace with the development of Al. The structure of Europe, with its different levels of power and institutions, is a brake on rapid decision-making But working more with experts can speed up decision-making

In defence and security: preserving EU autonomy and protecting against cyber-attacks via Al. To arm ourselves against threats from outside the EU, we need to strengthen cyber defence at the European level

Al must be a priority of the European institutions. Europe must be proud of its strengths and communicate them more effectively. We have an abundance of innovative projects that no one knows about. We need to communicate more with the general public and younger generations (eg. to promote training or jobs).

data.title:
The vision of this citizen panel is that the EU should build and strengthen its position in the world as follows (2/2)

Readily invest in the development of Al applications based on the strengths of the EU and its most important players. We encourage member states, but also private funds, to devote more of their budgets to the development of Al The resources currently being invested are not enough if we want to lead in this field

Avoid mutual competition between Member States

Be more ambitious in promoting and protecting European values and standards in the applications of Al. This is Europe's strength.

data.title:
We believe that deepfakes and fake news generated by Al are untrustworthy sources of information and have a significant impact on our society they can influence citizens, threaten the privacy of individuals (eg, by spreading fake nude images), destroy reputations or create fake reputations, and easily spread false information. This can encourage bullying. Therefore, we believe that deepfakes and fake news should be considered high risk and not low risk as currently stated in the Al Act. 

Moreover, just because there is legislation on illegal deepfake does not mean that the problem is solved for people and democracyThis is an urgent and important issue that should be at the top of the political and legal agenda both nationally and at the European level

We also want a regulatory framework to be implemented exclusively by EU political actors, so that the responsibilities are not fragmented across a variety of actors

data.title: It is important not to lose our human, soft skills. The focus needs to be on young people, who are already strongly influenced by AI systems (especially through social networks and platforms that use AI). They will have to live with these tools in the future. We therefore need to prepare them, to ensure that there is no gap between what we learn in school and what is needed in our adult personal and professional lives.

data.title:
Al should serve to help humans, not replace them

We believe that people should not only have the last word at the end of a decision-making process in which Al is used but that they must be involved throughout the process to explain or intervene. This is clearly important when Al systems are used without our explicit consent and when there is high risk, for example, in medical diagnosis or loan decisions

Transparency and trust are important and go hand in hand in this regard if people gain insight into how and why a decision was made, they will more readily accept the outcome

This is all the more important for people less familiar with Al, or who do not have access to it, so that they are not excluded from society
data.additional-credit-line: Messages on 'Human in the loop' and human contact

outputs.title:
Al should serve to help humans, not replace them

We believe that people should not only have the last word at the end of a decision-making process in which Al is used but that they must be involved throughout the process to explain or intervene. This is clearly important when Al systems are used without our explicit consent and when there is high risk, for example, in medical diagnosis or loan decisions

Transparency and trust are important and go hand in hand in this regard if people gain insight into how and why a decision was made, they will more readily accept the outcome

This is all the more important for people less familiar with Al, or who do not have access to it, so that they are not excluded from society
